Definition: from the base of G3582 (through the idea of scorching); arid; by implication, shrunken, earth (as opposed to water):--dry land, withered.
BiblicalUsage: There was a man which had his hand withered, and they asked Jesus whether it was lawful to heal on the sabbath, and He said to the man, stand forth.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the withered hand is the whole argument in miniature: a hand that cannot work, a day that cannot be broken, and a Lord who heals in front of the men waiting to accuse Him.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
